fact: UCC and Starlink (SpaceX) signed a five-year operating licence agreement in May 2026, with national gateway, local presence and device registration conditions.
Starlink announced commercial satellite internet service available in Uganda on 2 September 2026, with a residential 100 Mbps package at about US$54 a month.
Starlink launched commercial satellite internet in Uganda on 2 September 2026 after regulatory approval; Residential 100 Mbps costs Shs203,704 a month, kit entry cost about Shs2.3m.

MTN Uganda added Starlink satellite connectivity to its enterprise portfolio, an initial offer to enterprise customers in remote areas, reported 27 August 2026 (article date used, none given for the event).
UCC approved Starlink's provisional operational licence in May 2026, with national gateway, device registration and local office conditions.
Paratus Uganda became the first provider to launch Starlink LEO service in Uganda, reselling it to enterprise customers, announced Monday before the 25 August 2026 article.
UCC and Starlink signed a memorandum of understanding and operational licence agreement on 15 May 2026, per Red Pepper, clearing Starlink service in Uganda.
Starlink service went live in Uganda with Roke Telkom and Paratus Uganda the first providers to switch it on for enterprise customers, per Red Pepper (article date, no launch date given).
On 6 January 2026 UCC said Starlink had not met its requirements and that Starlink terminals were being imported and used illegally, per TechMoonshot.
By May 2026 Starlink held a provisional infrastructure and service licence in Uganda, with a condition of a national gateway in Uganda, per TechMoonshot.

Paratus said Starlink services had recently launched in Uganda, adding satellite connectivity for businesses where fixed infrastructure is limited, per TechTrendsKE (article date used, no launch date given).
UCC and Starlink signed a memorandum of understanding and an operational licence agreement in May 2026, per Space in Africa.

Roke Telkom and Paratus Uganda launched Starlink for Business in Uganda, with Paratus Uganda the first provider to offer Starlink commercially, on 24-month plans of 500GB to 2TB at 40-220 Mbps down, per Space in Africa.
Roke Telkom with Paratus Uganda launched Starlink enterprise connectivity, reselling Starlink LEO capacity to businesses, per Nile Post.

Agence Ecofin reports that Starlink's official availability map lists Uganda among 16 African markets marked 'Starting in 2026', shown as service coverage or regulatory authorisation pending, so not yet available in Uganda; no launch date given (article date used).

UCC states Starlink holds a provisional infrastructure and service licence to operate satellite services in Uganda, with conditions of a national gateway with local point of presence and local registration of all devices; no licence date given, article date used.

Daily Monitor reports UCC signed an MoU and a five-year provisional operational licence agreement with Starlink Services LLC 'last Friday' (Friday before the 20 May 2026 article, i.e. 15 May 2026), with landing rights authorisation to beam satellite signals within Uganda.
Daily Monitor reports that in December 2025 the government halted clearance of Starlink equipment into Uganda ahead of the 15 January 2026 elections.

Telecom Review Africa reports UCC and Starlink (SpaceX) signed an MoU and operational licence agreement authorising Starlink to begin operations in Uganda, with national gateway, physical point of presence and local office required; commercial launch still planned (article date used).

Connecting Africa reports UCC granted Starlink a provisional licence via an MoU and operational licence agreement, with a national gateway, device registration and staffed local office required; Starlink was still preparing to begin service (article date used).

UCC and Starlink (SpaceX) signed a licence agreement on 15 May 2026 at State House Entebbe, which The Independent reports as Uganda licensing Starlink to begin commercial operations, conditional on a local presence, a national gateway and device registration.

UCC and Starlink/SpaceX signed an MoU and operational licence agreement at State House Entebbe, and UCC handed over an operational certificate; the Ministry of ICT permanent secretary called it a provisional licence, with a national gateway, local office and device registration required (page posted 2026-05-18; signing date 2026-05-15 per the page's staging note).

UCC formally licensed Starlink on 15 May 2026 with an operational certificate handed to SpaceX; the licence requires a national gateway, a staffed local office and registration of all devices before commercial operations begin.
Uganda blocked unauthorised Starlink use in January 2026 and cut off users who had been running it on foreign SIM registrations.

UCC and Starlink/SpaceX signed an MoU and operational licence agreement at State House Entebbe on Friday 15 May 2026; UCC issued certification, and the Ministry of ICT permanent secretary described it as the provisional licence, with a national gateway, local office and device registration required.

UCC and Starlink signed an MoU and operational licence agreement witnessed by President Museveni, announced 15 May 2026, paving the way for Starlink to begin operations; service delivery had not yet begun.

Uganda Communications Commission and Starlink (SpaceX) signed an MoU and operational licence agreement on 15 May 2026, and the UCC Executive Director issued certification for Starlink's rollout; the licence requires a national gateway, a physical point of presence and a local office.

UCC stated on 10 January 2026 that Starlink's licensing application was still under regulatory review, no approval had been granted, and Starlink lacked authorisation to provide services in Uganda directly or through licensed entities; no retail launch was planned and satellite capacity is to be supplied wholesale through licensed operators such as Airtel Uganda.

UCC issued a directive on 1 January 2026 requiring Starlink to deploy geolocation controls against illegal use of its signals in Uganda; Starlink complied and UCC verified previously active terminals were offline.

Starlink told UCC in a 2 January 2026 letter that any Starlink usage in Uganda was unauthorised, that Starlink Uganda had never imported or distributed terminals, and that no Starlink terminals were operating in Uganda as of 1 January 2026; it accepted UCC's request to restrict its devices (document is paywalled, only headline and lead read).

Starlink shut down access to its service in Uganda on UCC instructions; a 1 January 2026 Starlink letter to UCC says the company is not authorised to operate in Uganda because its local entity has not been granted a licence, and terminals in use had been activated through neighbouring countries.

UCC corporate affairs director Fred Otunnu said Starlink was not yet licensed to operate in Uganda, and an army spokesman called it illegal; URA restricted import of Starlink equipment without CDF clearance by letter of 19 December 2025; Starlink had applied for a licence (UCC confirmed engagement in April 2025).
A table of Starlink availability by country lists Uganda as 2026 with licence approved (article date used, no licence date given).

Regulators granted Starlink a licence in Uganda conditional on a physical presence, a national gateway/ground station, in-country device registration and local technical and legal staff (article date used, no licence date given).
Starlink launched in Uganda in May 2026, per an Ookla study note excluding Uganda from its 23-country speed sample.

fact: UCC signed a Memorandum of Understanding and operational licence agreement with Starlink in May 2026, opening the door to satellite internet for underserved communities (per CEO.co.ug reporting the UCC Q2 2026 report).
In December 2025 Uganda's government restricted imports of Starlink satellite internet equipment.
On 1 January 2026 Starlink disabled its service for users in Uganda following a request from the UCC.

UCC and Starlink signed an MoU and operational licence agreement at State House Entebbe, witnessed by the President, clearing Starlink to operate in Uganda; conditions include a national gateway, local presence and staff, and registration of all devices activated in Uganda. Dated by the article's publication week (signing on a Thursday).
